concepts.def: A pre-recorded audio clip used inside another track.
Simulates a space — adds room or hall ambience.
Echoes the signal at a chosen time gap.
Equalisation — boosts or cuts frequency ranges.
Reduces dynamic range, evens out volume.
Position of sound in the stereo field (left to right).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sampling takes a piece of audio — a drum break, vocal phrase, vinyl crackle — and uses it as raw material. Producers chop samples up, pitch them, time-stretch them, then arrange them on a new groove.

Beware copyright: famous samples require clearance, otherwise the original songwriter may sue.

Reverb places the sound in a space — a tiny room, a cathedral, a metal plate. Used on vocals and snares for depth.

Delay repeats the signal at a chosen interval (1/8 note, 1/4 note). Set in time with the BPM for musical echoes — perfect for guitar solos.

EQ boosts or cuts frequencies. Cut around 200 Hz to remove muddy bass; boost 3–5 kHz for clarity on vocals.

Compression turns down the loudest parts so the whole track sits at a more even level — essential on vocals, bass and drum buses. Combined with EQ, this is the heart of mixing.
